plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (28-layer HfO2/SiO2 dual-band filter) based on prior iteration evidence. Best score plateaued at 0.819 then declined to 0.729, suggesting gradient optimizer trapped in local optima. Per feedback directives, I will: (1) switch to differential evolution with Latin Hypercube initialization, (2) expand thickness bounds to ±20% of observed min/max from iteration_07, (3) add a complementary 20-layer route to test if reduced complexity improves convergence, (4) include explicit robustness-weighted optimization. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_03' per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: 28-Layer Stack with Differential Evolution and Latin Hypercube Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Global optimization with differential evolution and Latin Hypercube sampling will escape local optima that trapped the gradient-based optimizer in prior iterations, achieving higher target scores by exploring multi-modal interference landscapes more thoroughly.
routes.design_principle: Replace gradient-based local search with population-based global search. Initialize thickness population using Latin Hypercube distribution spanning ±20% of iteration_07's observed thickness range (45-201 nm for HfO2, 45-73 nm for SiO2). Maintain alternating HfO2/SiO2 sequence on fused silica substrate.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 28 layer thicknesses (14 HfO2 + 14 SiO2), each independently optimizable within expanded bounds
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maintain robustness score > 0.35 under ±15% thickness perturbation
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds expanded to 40-240 nm for HfO2, 35-90 nm for SiO2 based on iteration_07 observations
Outermost layer should be SiO2 for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Global optimization explores configuration space more thoroughly than gradient descent for multi-modal problems
expected_advantages: Escapes local optima that limited prior gradient-based runs
Latin Hypercube ensures uniform coverage of thickness parameter space
Higher probability of finding globally optimal interference conditions
known_risks: Differential evolution requires more function evaluations, may need larger search budget
May converge slower in early generations before exploiting promising regions
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)|SiO2(2)|HfO2(3)|SiO2(4)|...|HfO2(27)|SiO2(28). Initialize 28 thickness variables using Latin Hypercube sampling with bounds: HfO2 layers 40-240 nm, SiO2 layers 35-90 nm. Use differential evolution optimizer with population size 50, mutation rate 0.8, crossover rate 0.9, maximum 500 generations. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band) and (mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band) with equal weights. Apply ±15% relative uniform thickness tolerance for robustness scoring. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for top 5 candidates. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Switched from gradient_thickness to differential_evolution optimizer per feedback directive. Expanded thickness bounds to ±20% of iteration_07 observed range (was 50-300 nm uniform, now 40-240 nm for HfO2, 35-90 nm for SiO2). Added Latin Hypercube initialization for better parameter space coverage.

routes.title: 20-Layer Reduced Complexity Stack with Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 28 to 20 will decrease optimization dimensionality, allowing the solver to converge more reliably to a high-quality solution. Quarter-wave initialization at band-center wavelengths provides physically-motivated starting point that gradient or global optimizers can refine.
routes.design_principle: Use 10 bilayers (20 total layers) instead of 14 bilayers. Initialize HfO2 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 375 nm (UV band center, ~55 nm physical), SiO2 layers at quarter-wave for 1350 nm (SWIR band center, ~230 nm physical). This creates a chirped-like starting condition favoring both bands.

manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count = 20 (well within 30-layer limit, reduces deposition time and stress)

theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity maximizes when layers have optical thickness n×t = λ/4
Reduced parameter dimensionality improves optimizer convergence for non-convex problems
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to 8 fewer optimization variables
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Lower total thickness reduces stress and deposition time
known_risks: Fewer layers may limit achievable bandwidth for both bands
May not reach same peak performance as 28-layer if bandwidth requirements demand more interfaces

routes.title: 28-Layer Stack with Robustness-Weighted Multi-Objective Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Explicitly weighting robustness in the objective function during optimization (not just as post-hoc evaluation) will produce designs that maintain performance under thickness variations, addressing the robustness score variability seen in prior iterations (0.317-0.498).
routes.design_principle: Modify objective function to include robustness as a tertiary optimization target alongside the two spectral bands. Use a composite merit function: 0.4×T_SWIR + 0.4×R_UV + 0.2×Robustness. This biases the optimizer toward thickness combinations that are less sensitive to fabrication variations.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 28 layer thicknesses (14 HfO2 + 14 SiO2), each independently optimizable within bounds 50-250 nm for HfO2, 40-100 nm for SiO2
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band (weight 0.4)
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band (weight 0.4)
Maximize robustness score under ±15% thickness perturbation (weight 0.2)
manufacturing_considerations: Explicit robustness weighting targets fabrication tolerance from start
Outermost SiO2 layer ≥50 nm for environmental durability per evidence
Thickness bounds chosen to avoid extremely thin layers that are difficult to control
theory_basis: Multi-objective optimization balances competing goals during search rather than sequentially
Robustness-weighted designs maintain performance under realistic fabrication variations
expected_advantages: Produces designs with inherently higher tolerance to thickness errors
Addresses robustness score variability from prior iterations (0.317-0.498 range)
May find thickness combinations that are less sensitive to interference condition shifts
known_risks: Explicit robustness weighting may reduce peak spectral performance
Requires additional function evaluations for robustness calculation at each generation
